elements.element: Vendor has a duty to defend against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause requires TrueLink to “indemnify and hold Client harmless” but contains no duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor has a duty to indemnify against the covered claims.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires TrueLink to indemnify and hold Client harmless from claims, actions, expenses, losses and liabilities.

elements.element: Customer and its affiliates are protected indemnified parties.
elements.evidence: The protected parties expressly include “Client” and “its affiliates,” along with additional Client representatives.

elements.element: The indemnity covers third-party claims for each required indemnity trigger.
elements.evidence: The opening language covers “all claims” and therefore includes third-party claims; the IP trigger also expressly refers to an allegation concerning a right “of a third party.”

elements.element: The indemnity covers allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Subclause (ii) covers allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any third-party intellectual property right.

elements.element: The indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Subclause (iii) expressly covers “TrueLink's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: The indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subclause (iv) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Client Proprietary Information, or borrower or loan data when caused by TrueLink.

elements.element: The indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subclause (v) expressly covers “TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No notice procedure appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure gives Vendor control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no defense or settlement-control provision.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no indemnity obligation on Client, so no Customer indemnity exceeds the permitted scope.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: TrueLink indemnifies Client, and subclause (ii) expressly covers allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate a third party's intellectual property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Client modifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Client specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies permit Vendor to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No procure-right remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies permit Vendor to modify the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies permit Vendor to replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing equivalents.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies require an appropriate refund if the procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no indemnity cap or reference to a three-times-annual-fees super-cap.

result.reason: The redline adds the required IP, breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data incident, and gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct triggers, but omits the defense duty and all required indemnity procedures. It also omits every fallback exclusion, remedy, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. Because neither position is complete, the redline is not minimal to a complete level. It otherwise preserves the original Vendor indemnity without introducing a substantive contradiction, although the wording is awkward and duplicative, including “arising from or relating to any (i) any claim” and the repeated use of “harmless.”
